title: Sweep atomicwrite users that tmp+rename linkable .evolve/ state files without resolving the worktree symlink (cycle-999 sever class)
evidence: Follow-up of statejson-latent-unresolved-writers how_to_apply step (3). Cycle 1690 delivered steps (1) and (2): statemap.ResolveWriteTarget is exported, core.SealCycle locks the resolved <canonical>.lock, and failurelog's atomicWriteJSON seam renames onto the resolved target.

Step (3) was deferred in scout prose only (triage-decision.json deferred: []), and a PASS landing consumes the whole lane item through ship/postship.go committedInboxIDs. This record carries step (3) forward so it does not vanish with the parent (cycle-1690 audit M1).

Cycle-1690 Discovery Scan: other atomicwrite callers write .evolve/ state-adjacent files. Any of them reached with a worktree-linked path would replace the link with a regular file, the cycle-999 sever.
how_to_apply: (1) Enumerate every atomicwrite caller whose target can be a worktree-linked .evolve/ file (state.json and its siblings the worktree provisioner symlinks). (2) For each one, route the write through statemap.ResolveWriteTarget, or add an opt-in resolve-symlinks mode to atomicwrite and use it at those sites. (3) Pin each migrated writer with a symlink regression test that mirrors statemap_integrity_test.go.
acceptance: Every writer of .evolve/state.json, ledger.jsonl or cycle-state.json — the three files core/worktree.go:295-302 symlinks into a worktree — writes through statemap.ResolveWriteTarget regardless of implementation. The remaining unresolved writers are adapters/storage WriteState / WriteCycleState (statejson.go:51-111) and UpdateState (updatestate.go:41-87), which rename onto the UNRESOLVED path via the private writeJSONAtomic (statejson.go:219-255). Keep storage and statemap as separate paths (statemap.go:1-21 documents why); only resolve the write target.

Each migrated writer has a regression test that is RED on the pre-fix code, covering an absolute link, a relative link and a dangling link: after the write the symlink is still a symlink and the canonical file holds the new bytes.

The atomicwrite-caller inventory is recorded in the build report: none of the ~45 production atomicwrite.Bytes/JSON callers targets one of the three linked files (verified 2026-09-26) — record it, do not migrate them.
connects_to: go/internal/core/worktree.go:295-302 (the three files a worktree symlinks)
surface_note: 2026-09-26 console premise audit (read-only, against main 4bd6f2ee): PARTIAL — steps 1-2 landed in 4bd6f2ee (statemap.ResolveWriteTarget; reset.go SealCycle; failurelog atomicWriteJSON). As filed, step 3 (every atomicwrite caller) had ZERO live targets; the real remaining writers of the linked files are in adapters/storage (latent today: every production writer uses the canonical evolveDir; the worktree-rooted storage.New in cli/guardcmd/guard.go:295-297 only reads). Retargeted files[] and acceptance accordingly.
